title: U.S. House, District 21
what_it_does: Represents Florida's 21th Congressional District in the U.S. House of Representatives; votes on federal laws and spending.
verified_ballot_note: Roster from CBS12 (James Martin wins Democratic primary; Mast unopposed) and Ballotpedia (Robert Ott, NPA, in general election). County makeup under the 2026 map was not captured in search snippets (the pre-2026 district covered Martin and St. Lucie counties and part of Palm Beach County). Sources: https://cbs12.com/news/election/florida-election-news-james-martin-wins-democratic-primary-will-face-brian-mast-in-florida-21-congressional-district-bernard-taylor-concedes-november-3-matchup ; https://ballotpedia.org/Florida's_21st_Congressional_District_election,_2026 Florida adopted a new congressional map (passed Apr 29, 2026, signed May 4, 2026) that reworked 21 of 28 districts; county descriptions here reflect post-redistricting reporting where found (https://www.wusf.org/politics-issues/2026-05-06/breakdown-changes-for-florida-new-congressional-map).

candidates.name: Brian Mast
candidates.photo_source: congress.gov member portrait (bioguide ID from memory, unverified)
candidates.occupation: U.S. Representative (since 2017); chair, House Foreign Affairs Committee
candidates.background: Brian Mast, an Army veteran who lost both legs in Afghanistan, has served in the U.S. House since 2017 (first in the 18th District, then the 21st after 2022 redistricting) and chairs the House Foreign Affairs Committee. He was unopposed in the Aug. 18, 2026 Republican primary.
